sections.report-regulatory:
D10 Regulatory currency. Statutory references reflect the law and guidance as at 2026-10-08 for the pathway and lodgement date shown. Under the Planning Act 2026, consents lodged before 30 October 2026 are processed under the RMA as it stood immediately before 30 September 2026, and those lodged later are processed under the amended RMA as at lodgement. The specified transition date to the new planning system has not been set. This report is not legal or planning advice. Confirm the applicable provisions at lodgement.
D11 Authorities. Since 7 May 2026 Auckland Council is the road controlling authority for Auckland roads (Local Government (Auckland Council) Act 2009 s47), with local boards exercising specified powers on local and collector roads and Auckland Transport continuing as the transport CCO for public transport. AUP provisions that still refer to Auckland Transport are quoted as written. Confirm the reviewing and approving body for this application.

sections.report-modelling:
Spare Construct assigns peak-hour vehicle demand (gravity distribution with gateway through-traffic) to the network by conjugate Frank-Wolfe user equilibrium, with BPR link times (α 0.15, β 4) and HCM 6 / Akçelik junction delay. Background growth: compound, 2.0% a year from 2026. Convergence target: relative gap 0.010% with the TAG M3.1 stability rule, at most 200 iterations. Full inputs are in Appendix A.

Every stored run converged to its target (Appendix B).

MSM consistency not checked: AT ITA v2 s4.2.1.1 expects consistency with MSM forecasts where appropriate.

D7 Regional consistency. The AT ITA Guidelines 2025 v2 expect detailed modelling to be consistent with regional MSM forecasts where appropriate. Where this report states that MSM consistency was not checked, the forecasts should be reconciled with MSM or Auckland Forecasting Centre outputs before lodgement for any proposal with network-wide effects.

sections.report-junctions: The junction flow-scale test (+10% on every movement) follows this section, then turning movement diagrams for the key junctions; per-turn movement summaries are in Appendix C. The sensitivity pack (section 4.6) re-runs the whole network with trip rates and total demand ±10% and background growth ±50%.

Junctions whose degree of saturation crosses the practical limit when flows rise by 10%:

sections.report-conclusion:
With the proposal, all 3 assessed junctions operate within practical DoS in the 2031 AM and PM peaks; the worst is Main Road / Side 6N (DoS 0.79, LoS B, AM peak). Junction results are indicative (HCM 6 / Akcelik-based), not SIDRA output.

D1 Screening status. Spare Construct is a browser-based sketch and screening tool. It is not an approved regional transport model and it is not the Auckland Forecasting Centre Macro Strategic Model (MSM). Its results are indicative and are intended to scope, test and support a transport assessment. Any person who relies on these outputs in evidence remains responsible for complying with the Code of Conduct for Expert Witnesses (Environment Court Practice Note 2023, section 9), including stating the assumptions and data relied on, the uncertainty in the results, and appropriate sensitivity and uncertainty analyses for any model. D3 Junction results. Junction delay, degree of saturation, level of service and queue results are calculated by Spare Construct using HCM 6 / Akcelik-based methods. They are indicative and are not SIDRA output. Any junction result relied on for a consent decision, signal design (ATOC Traffic Signals Design Guidelines) or condition should be confirmed in SIDRA or another tool accepted by the road controlling authority.
D4 Economics. The benefit-cost ratio is an indicative screening estimate following NZTA Monetised Benefits and Costs Manual v1.7.5 conventions. It is equivalent to an Indicative Efficiency Rating, not a funding-approval BCR. It is not MBCM-compliant unless the full procedures are applied to a model calibrated and validated to the NZTA Transport Model Development Guidelines and independently reviewed. Regulatory contextauto

D10 Regulatory currency. Statutory references reflect the law and guidance as at 2026-10-08 for the pathway and lodgement date shown. Under the Planning Act 2026, consents lodged before 30 October 2026 are processed under the RMA as it stood immediately before 30 September 2026, and those lodged later are processed under the amended RMA as at lodgement. The specified transition date to the new planning system has not been set. This report is not legal or planning advice. Confirm the applicable provisions at lodgement.
D11 Authorities. Since 7 May 2026 Auckland Council is the road controlling authority for Auckland roads (Local Government (Auckland Council) Act 2009 s47), with local boards exercising specified powers on local and collector roads and Auckland Transport continuing as the transport CCO for public transport. AUP provisions that still refer to Auckland Transport are quoted as written. Confirm the reviewing and approving body for this application.

TMDG criteria are not a pass/fail checklist; meeting them does not by itself make a model fit for purpose (TMDG s5.8).

Scope and proportionalitymixed

The RR 422 scope (Simple, Moderate, Broad or Extensive) has not been chosen (Report tab).

Limitationsmixed

Executive summarymixed

  • The development generates about 558 veh/h in the AM peak hour and 612 veh/h in the PM peak hour (vehicle trips, 2031, Option: signals at Side 2).
  • 3 junctions assessed; the highest degree of saturation is Main Road / Side 6N in the AM peak (DoS 0.79, LoS B). Indicative, not SIDRA output.
  • Extent of effects (AT ITA s4.2.1.1): AM peak 1 link direction and 1 junction over the 5%/10% thresholds; PM peak 1 link direction and 1 junction over the 5%/10% thresholds.
  • Model status: AM Uncalibrated, PM Uncalibrated; every stored run converged.

4 Transport assessment

4.1 Assessment scenariosauto

Assessed in this report: Option: signals at Side 2 against Base case.

4.2 Model description and calibration summaryauto

Spare Construct assigns peak-hour vehicle demand (gravity distribution with gateway through-traffic) to the network by conjugate Frank-Wolfe user equilibrium, with BPR link times (α 0.15, β 4) and HCM 6 / Akçelik junction delay. Background growth: compound, 2.0% a year from 2026. Convergence target: relative gap 0.010% with the TAG M3.1 stability rule, at most 200 iterations. Full inputs are in Appendix A.

Every stored run converged to its target (Appendix B).

MSM consistency not checked: AT ITA v2 s4.2.1.1 expects consistency with MSM forecasts where appropriate.

D7 Regional consistency. The AT ITA Guidelines 2025 v2 expect detailed modelling to be consistent with regional MSM forecasts where appropriate. Where this report states that MSM consistency was not checked, the forecasts should be reconciled with MSM or Auckland Forecasting Centre outputs before lodgement for any proposal with network-wide effects.

4.2.2 Extent of effectsauto

The extent sites are not stored on the scenario yet, so the assessed junctions are Spare Construct's own selection. Store the extent test (junctions feature) to use it for the SIDRA export and this report.

4.2.3 Junction performanceauto

The junction flow-scale test (+10% on every movement) follows this section, then turning movement diagrams for the key junctions; per-turn movement summaries are in Appendix C. The sensitivity pack (section 4.6) re-runs the whole network with trip rates and total demand ±10% and background growth ±50%.

4.2.3.1 Junction flow-scale test (+10%)

Junctions whose degree of saturation crosses the practical limit when flows rise by 10%:

  • Base case, AM peak: Main Road / Side 2N / Side 2S (North: Side 2N (T)); Main Road / Side 6N (West: Main Road (L))
  • Option: signals at Side 2, AM peak: Main Road / Side 6N (West: Main Road (L))

Flow-scale test: TTOC-06 Traffic Signals Modelling Guidelines. Junctions are re-evaluated at flows × 1.10 with each run's signal timings; routes are not re-assigned. HCM 6 / Akcelik-based, indicative; not SIDRA output.

4.2.3.2 Turning movement diagrams

Modelled peak-hour turning volumes, AM (PM), rounded to the nearest 5 veh/h. HCM 6 / Akcelik-based, indicative; not SIDRA output.

4.6 Sensitivity testsauto

The sensitivity pack has not been run (Report tab › Run the sensitivity pack). AT ITA s3.6.1(v) and the Practice Note s9.3(a)(x) expect sensitivity testing.

4.7 Indicative economicsauto

Indicative economics compare a transport option (the mitigation scenario) with the do-minimum (the scenario with the proposal), at the same travel demand. The development itself is not a transport option, so no benefit-cost ratio is given for it. Create a mitigation scenario (Scenarios › Create assessment set) or choose one in the Report tab.

What each option changes against Base case:

5.2 Staging triggersauto

Run the staging test in the Report tab: it runs the proposal at 10% build-out steps and finds the first increment where an assessed junction fails.

5.3 Conditions and monitoringmixed

Author to complete. Draft condition parameters (RMA s108, s108AA): for each measure in Table M1, the effect it addresses (its nexus), the trigger, who delivers it and how compliance is shown.
Author to complete. Monitoring and travel plan (RMA Sch 4 cl 6(1)(g); AUP E27.9(2)): what is monitored, when, the threshold, and what happens when it is crossed.

6 Conclusion

6.1 Conclusionmixed

With the proposal, all 3 assessed junctions operate within practical DoS in the 2031 AM and PM peaks; the worst is Main Road / Side 6N (DoS 0.79, LoS B, AM peak). Junction results are indicative (HCM 6 / Akcelik-based), not SIDRA output.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
# Spare Construct to SIDRA INTERSECTION 11 volume loader (New Zealand setup)
#
# D1 Screening status
#   Spare Construct is a browser-based sketch and screening tool. It is not an approved regional transport model and
#   it is not the Auckland Forecasting Centre Macro Strategic Model (MSM). Its results are indicative and are
#   intended to scope, test and support a transport assessment. They must be reviewed, and where necessary confirmed
#   with approved tools, by a suitably qualified transport planner or traffic engineer before they are relied on in
#   any resource consent, plan change, notice of requirement, Fast-track application or funding decision.
# D12 Hand-over
#   This export is prepared for use in SIDRA Intersection. Results produced in that tool, not the Spare Construct
#   estimates, should be reported where the tool is required or accepted by the reviewing authority.
#
# Requires licensed SIDRA 11, 64-bit Python, pythonnet, .NET 8; close the project in SIDRA first; untested against a live install.
#
# Made by Spare Construct on 2026-10-21 for scenario Option: signals at Side 2 (2031); periods AM, PM; 56 movements at 3 sites.
# Volumes are modelled demand in vehicles per hour (light and heavy vehicles), not PCU and not throughput, from a
# Spare Construct sketch model. Spare Construct junction results are HCM 6 / Akcelik-based, indicative and not SIDRA output.
#
# Usage
#   py -3 load_corridor_volumes.py --dry-run                print the planned SIDRA API calls; SIDRA is not needed
#   py -3 load_corridor_volumes.py PROJECT.sipx             add or update sites in an existing SIDRA project
#   py -3 load_corridor_volumes.py PROJECT.sipx --create    create the project first
#   --csv corridor-sidra-volumes.csv                        read the volumes from the CSV instead of the copy below
#
# Update mode: a site in the same folder whose Intersection ID is the Spare Construct site id keeps its lane and phasing
# coding. Its volumes, peak flow factors, unit time for volumes and peak flow period are overwritten; every movement
# between its legs is set to 0 first, so a movement with no traffic now (a banned turn, a changed network) does not
# keep an old volume. New sites get one leg per Spare Construct leg with default NZ geometry, which you must check and code.
# A peak flow factor from a turning count's 15-minute peak hour factor comes with a 15-minute peak flow period.
# Leg and turn codes follow SIDRA drive-on-left conventions: legs S 0, SE 1, E 2, NE 3, N 4, NW 5, W 6, SW 7
# (named by where traffic comes from); turns U, L3, L2, L1, T1, R1, R2, R3.
# Volumes already include growth to the scenario year, so growth_pct is 0.

NUMERIC = ('lat', 'lng', 'site_type', 'origin_leg', 'dest_leg', 'lv_veh_h', 'hv_veh_h', 'pff_pct', 'unit_time_min', 'peak_flow_period_min', 'growth_pct')
RETURNS = {'OpenProject': 'project', 'CreateAndOpenProject': 'project', 'AddSiteFolder': 'folder', 'AddSite': 'site'}


class DryRun(object):
    """Stands in for the SIDRA API: prints each call and assignment instead of making it."""

    def __init__(self, name):
        object.__setattr__(self, '_name', name)

    def __getattr__(self, attr):
        return DryRun(self._name + '.' + attr)

    def __setattr__(self, attr, value):
        print('%s.%s = %r' % (self._name, attr, value))

    def __call__(self, *args):
        print('%s(%s)' % (self._name, ', '.join(repr(a) for a in args)))
        return DryRun(RETURNS.get(self._name.split('.')[-1], 'result'))

    def __getitem__(self, key):
        k = ', '.join(repr(x) for x in key) if isinstance(key, tuple) else repr(key)
        return DryRun('%s[%s]' % (self._name, k))


def read_csv(path):
    with open(path, newline='', encoding='utf-8-sig') as f:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))
    for r in rows:
        for k in NUMERIC:
            if r.get(k, '') != '':
                r[k] = float(r[k]) if k in ('lat', 'lng') else int(float(r[k]))
    return rows


def group(rows):
    """One SIDRA site per Spare Construct site and period, with its legs and movements."""
    sites = {}
    for r in rows:
        key = (r['period'], str(r['site_id']))
        s = sites.get(key)
        if s is None:
            s = sites[key] = {'row': r, 'legs': set(), 'moves': []}
        s['legs'].add(int(r['origin_leg']))
        s['legs'].add(int(r['dest_leg']))
        s['moves'].append(r)
    return sites


def load_api():
    if sys.maxsize <= 2 ** 32:
        sys.exit('Use 64-bit Python: SIDRA 11 is a 64-bit application.')
    try:
        import winreg
        key = winreg.OpenKey(winreg.HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE, r'SOFTWARE\SIDRA SOLUTIONS\SIDRA INTERSECTION 11')
        loc = winreg.QueryValueEx(key, 'InstallLocation')[0]
    except OSError:
        sys.exit('SIDRA INTERSECTION 11 was not found in the registry. Install SIDRA 11, or run with --dry-run.')
    try:
        from pythonnet import set_runtime
        from clr_loader import get_coreclr
        set_runtime(get_coreclr(runtime_config=os.path.join(loc, 'SIDRASolutions.SI.API.runtimeconfig.json')))
        import clr
    except ImportError:
        sys.exit('pythonnet is missing. Install it with: py -3 -m pip install pythonnet')
    sys.path.append(loc)
    clr.AddReference(os.path.join(loc, 'SIDRASolutions.SI.API.dll'))
    from SIDRASolutions.SI.API import SIAPI
    return SIAPI()


def existing_sites(project):
    """Sites already in the project, keyed by (folder name, Intersection ID)."""
    found, folders = {}, {}
    if isinstance(project, DryRun):
        return found, folders
    for folder in getattr(project, 'SiteFolders', None) or []:
        folders[str(folder.Name)] = folder
        for site in getattr(folder, 'Sites', None) or []:
            found[(str(folder.Name), str(site.Intersectionid))] = site
    return found, folders


def set_volumes(site, moves):
    for m in moves:
        od = site.MovementVehicleODs[int(m['origin_leg']), int(m['dest_leg'])]
        od.MovementVehicleODMCs[1].Volume = int(m['lv_veh_h'])
        od.MovementVehicleODMCs[2].Volume = int(m['hv_veh_h'])
        od.Peak_flow_factor = int(m['pff_pct'])


def site_legs(site_id, legs=()):
    return sorted(set(int(k) for k in LEG_LANES.get(site_id, {})) | set(int(x) for x in legs))


def clear_volumes(site, legs):
    """Update mode: set every movement between the site's legs to 0 before the new volumes are written."""
    for o in legs:
        for d in legs:
            try:
                od = site.MovementVehicleODs[o, d]
            except Exception:  # no such movement on this site
                continue
            if od is None:
                continue
            for mc in (1, 2):
                try:
                    od.MovementVehicleODMCs[mc].Volume = 0
                except Exception:
                    pass


def main(argv=None, api=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='Load Spare Construct turning volumes into a SIDRA INTERSECTION 11 project (New Zealand setup).')
    ap.add_argument('project', nargs='?', help='the .sipx project file')
    ap.add_argument('--create', action='store_true', help='create the project first')
    ap.add_argument('--csv', help='read volumes from this CSV (corridor-sidra-volumes.csv) instead of the embedded copy')
    ap.add_argument('--dry-run', action='store_true', help='print the planned SIDRA API calls without SIDRA')
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    print(NOTICE)
    rows = read_csv(a.csv) if a.csv else DATA
    if not rows:
        print('No volumes to load. Export again from Spare Construct after running the model.')
        return 1
    if not a.project and not a.dry_run:
        ap.error('give the .sipx project file, or --dry-run')
    if NOT_CONVERGED:
        print('WARNING: ' + NOT_CONVERGED + '. These volumes are not fit to rely on.')
    path = a.project or 'corridor.sipx'
    if api is None:
        api = DryRun('api') if a.dry_run else load_api()
    project = api.CreateAndOpenProject(path, 'Spare Construct ' + SCENARIO) if a.create else api.OpenProject(path)
    if project is None:
        project = getattr(api, 'Project', None)
    if project is None:
        sys.exit('SIDRA could not open %s. Close it in SIDRA and check the path.' % path)
    found, folders = existing_sites(project)
    made = updated = cleared = 0
    groups = group(rows)
    for (period, site_id), s in sorted(groups.items()):
        r = s['row']
        fname = 'Spare Construct %s %s' % (SCENARIO, period)
        folder = folders.get(fname)
        if folder is None:
            folder = folders[fname] = project.AddSiteFolder(fname)
        site = found.get((fname, site_id))
        if site is None:
            site = folder.AddSite(int(r['site_type']), NZ_SETUP)
            site.Name = '%s (%s)' % (r['site_name'], period)
            site.Intersectionid = site_id
            try:
                site.MapCoordinate.Latitude = float(r['lat'])
                site.MapCoordinate.Longitude = float(r['lng'])
            except Exception as e:  # MapCoordinate may be a value type in the API
                print('Could not set the map position of %s: %s' % (site_id, e))
            lanes = LEG_LANES.get(site_id, {})
            for leg in sorted(s['legs']):
                site.AddLegWithLanes(leg, int(lanes.get(str(leg), 1)))
            site.UpdateGeometryData()
            made += 1
        else:
            clear_volumes(site, site_legs(site_id, s['legs']))
            updated += 1
        site.Unittimeforvolumes = int(r['unit_time_min'])
        site.Peakflowperiod = int(r['peak_flow_period_min'])
        set_volumes(site, s['moves'])
    # a site in this export with no traffic at all in a period: clear its old volumes too
    prefix, periods = 'Spare Construct %s ' % SCENARIO, set(str(r['period']) for r in rows)
    for (fname, site_id), site in sorted(found.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[0]):
        period = fname[len(prefix):] if fname.startswith(prefix) else None
        if period in periods and site_id in LEG_LANES and (period, site_id) not in groups:
            clear_volumes(site, site_legs(site_id))
            cleared += 1
    api.SaveProject()
    print('Done: %d sites created, %d updated and %d set to no traffic in %s. Lanes and phasing of existing sites were kept.' % (made, updated, cleared, path))
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

# Load Spare Construct ITA data pack CSVs in Python (standard library only).
# Every CSV is UTF-8 with a BOM, and its first row is Disclaimer D1: skip it.

import csv, sys

def load(path):
    with open(path, encoding='utf-8-sig', newline='') as f:
        rows = list(csv.reader(f))
    if rows and rows[0] and rows[0][0].startswith('#'):
        rows = rows[1:]
    head, body = rows[0], rows[1:]
    return [dict(zip(head, r)) for r in body]

if __name__ == '__main__':
    path = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 'links.csv'
    data = load(path)
    print(f'{len(data)} rows from {path}')
    for row in data[:10]:
        print(row)
